title: Gas laws and thermodynamics
summary: Pressure, the mole and the ideal gas law, the kinetic model of an ideal gas, and (HL) the first and second laws of thermodynamics, entropy and heat engines.

keyterms.definition: Force per unit area acting normally on a surface, p = F/A, in pascals (Pa).
Amount of substance containing N_A = 6.02 × 10²³ particles.
A model gas with point particles, no intermolecular forces except in elastic collisions; obeys pV = nRT exactly.
pV = nRT = Nk_BT, where T is the absolute temperature in kelvin.
k_B = R/N_A = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹; links particle energy to temperature.

keyterms.term: Mean kinetic energy of a particle
keyterms.definition: For an ideal gas, average translational KE = (3/2)k_BT.
Q = ΔU + W: heat supplied equals increase in internal energy plus work done by the gas.
A process with no heat transfer (Q = 0); for a monatomic ideal gas pV^(5/3) is constant.
A process at constant temperature, so ΔU = 0 for an ideal gas and Q = W.
A measure of disorder; ΔS = ΔQ/T for heat transferred reversibly. It never decreases for an isolated system.
The entropy of an isolated system never decreases; no engine can convert heat completely into work.
Maximum efficiency of a heat engine between reservoirs at T_h and T_c: η = 1 − T_c/T_h.

questions.prompt: A fixed mass of ideal gas at constant temperature has its volume halved. Its pressure
questions.explanation: Boyle’s law (pV constant at constant T): halving V doubles p.

questions.text: A gas is heated at constant volume from 300 K to 450 K. Its pressure increases by a factor of ___.
questions.explanation: At constant V, p ∝ T: 450/300 = 1.5. Temperatures must be in kelvin.

questions.statement: In the ideal gas law, temperature may be entered in degrees Celsius.
questions.explanation: pV = nRT requires absolute temperature in kelvin; at 0 °C the gas still has pressure.

questions.prompt: How many moles are in 0.024 m³ of ideal gas at 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa and 300 K? (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)
Match each gas law to its statement.

pairs.right: V ∝ n at constant p and T

questions.explanation: All are special cases of pV = nRT.

questions.prompt: According to kinetic theory, what causes the pressure of a gas on a container wall?
options: The rate of change of momentum of particles colliding with the wall
questions.explanation: Each collision reverses the normal momentum; the total force per unit area from many collisions is the pressure.

questions.text: The average translational kinetic energy of a gas particle at 300 K is ___ × 10⁻²¹ J (k_B = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹).

questions.statement: Real gases behave most like an ideal gas at low pressure and high temperature.
questions.explanation: Particles are then far apart (negligible volume) and fast (intermolecular forces matter less).

questions.prompt: The internal energy of an ideal monatomic gas consists of
options: only the kinetic energy of its particles
questions.explanation: There are no intermolecular forces in an ideal gas, so U = (3/2)nRT is entirely kinetic.

questions.prompt: Order the reasoning for why heating a gas at constant volume raises its pressure.
items: Particles hit the walls more often and with greater momentum change
Force per unit area on the walls increases
questions.explanation: Both collision rate and momentum change per collision increase.

lessons.title: Thermodynamic processes and the first law

questions.prompt: A gas absorbs 500 J of heat and does 200 J of work on its surroundings. Its internal energy changes by

questions.text: A gas expands at a constant pressure of 2.0 × 10⁵ Pa from 0.010 m³ to 0.030 m³. The work done by the gas is ___ kJ.

questions.statement: In an isothermal expansion of an ideal gas, all the heat absorbed is converted into work done by the gas.
questions.explanation: T is constant so ΔU = 0, and Q = W.

questions.prompt: In a rapid adiabatic compression of a gas, its temperature
questions.explanation: Q = 0, and work is done ON the gas (W negative), so ΔU = −W > 0 and the temperature rises.

questions.prompt: Match each process to its defining condition.
questions.explanation: Each process fixes one quantity, simplifying Q = ΔU + W.

questions.prompt: On a p–V diagram, the work done by a gas during a cycle equals
options: the area enclosed by the loop
the area under the highest curve only
questions.explanation: Net work is the area enclosed; ΔU over a full cycle is zero because the gas returns to its initial state.

questions.text: For a monatomic ideal gas undergoing an adiabatic change, p V^___ is constant.
questions.explanation: The adiabatic relation for a monatomic ideal gas is pV^(5/3) = constant.

questions.statement: An adiabatic curve on a p–V diagram is less steep than an isothermal curve through the same point.
questions.explanation: Adiabatic curves are steeper because temperature also changes in the same direction as pressure.

questions.prompt: A gas is compressed at constant temperature. Which statement is correct?
options: It releases heat equal to the work done on it
questions.explanation: ΔU = 0, so Q = W; W is negative (work done on the gas), so Q is negative: heat leaves.

questions.prompt: The internal energy of 2.0 mol of monatomic ideal gas rises when its temperature rises by 10 K. By how much? (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)

lessons.title: Entropy, the second law and heat engines

questions.prompt: What is the maximum efficiency of an engine operating between 600 K and 300 K?

questions.statement: A heat engine can convert all the heat it absorbs into work if it is frictionless.
questions.explanation: The second law (Kelvin form) forbids it: some heat must always be rejected to a cold reservoir.

questions.text: 1200 J of heat flows reversibly into a reservoir at 400 K. Its entropy increases by ___ J K⁻¹.

questions.prompt: Heat flows spontaneously from a hot body to a cold body. Why does this increase total entropy?
options: The cold body gains more entropy (Q/T_c) than the hot body loses (Q/T_h)
questions.explanation: Since T_c < T_h, Q/T_c > Q/T_h, so the net entropy change is positive.

questions.prompt: Match each part of a heat engine to its role.
questions.explanation: A heat engine turns part of the heat flow from hot to cold into work.

questions.statement: The entropy of a system can decrease if the entropy of its surroundings increases by at least as much.
questions.explanation: Only the total entropy of an isolated system cannot decrease; a refrigerator lowers the entropy inside but raises it more outside.

questions.text: An engine takes in 1000 J and rejects 700 J each cycle. Its efficiency is ___%.

questions.prompt: Which processes make up a Carnot cycle?
questions.explanation: The Carnot cycle is the idealized reversible cycle with the highest possible efficiency between two temperatures.

questions.prompt: Statistically, entropy is related to the number of microstates Ω by
questions.explanation: More ways to arrange the particles (more microstates) means higher entropy.

questions.prompt: Order the stages of a Carnot cycle starting at the hottest, smallest-volume state.
items: Adiabatic compression, heating back to T_h
questions.explanation: Heat enters during the hot isothermal and leaves during the cold isothermal.
